description.narrative:
SMP _ Production <(>&<)> Technical Lead _ Kompong Thom <(>&<)> Lumphat: Activity 1.1: Conduct needs assessments and select farmer groups (ACs/PGs): This foundational activity ensures that project interventions are targeted and effective. A team from SMP will conduct field visits to Kampong Thom and Lumphat to engage with potential ACs and PGs. A structured needs assessment will be carried outto evaluate their current production practices, institutional capacity, market linkages, and commitment to the project. Based on clear selection criteria, the most suitable groups will be chosen to participate in the pilot. The budget covers travel, per diems forSMP staff, and per diems to ensure the participation of AC and PG members in initial consultations.
Activity 1.2: Deliver comprehensive technical training on Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), climate-smart agriculture, and pest management. Activity 1.2: Comprehensive Technical Training Program SMP will lead the implementation of a comprehensive technical trainingprogram targeting 100 farmers across 3-4 Cashew Nut Producer Groups (CNPGs). The training program will cover advanced Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) including climate-smart agriculture techniques, integrated pest management, proper pruning and graftingmethods, and efficient harvesting techniques. The training will be delivered through a combination of classroom sessions, field demonstrations, and farmer-to-farmer learning exchanges. The training program will be structured in three phases: foundationaltraining (months 4-6), advanced techniques (months 7-9), and peer learning and mentoring (months 10-12). Each farmer will receive a minimum of 40 hours of training across the project period, with ongoing technical support provided through monthly fieldvisits by SMP technical staff. The SMP will conduct logistical assessment of biomass collection <(>&<)> storage in two locations and provide training to help farmers use composting and biochar fertilizer. Then supporting the farmers to install bio char -compostfertilizer through training and organize demonstration of cashew fruit.
Activity 1.3: Establish and manage post-harvest demonstration sites. Post-harvest loss in Kampong Thom is high because farmers dry nuts on the ground, have poor storage, and don’tcontrol moisture. This causes quality issues, contamination, and inconsistent grades. Lower quality forces farmers to sell cheaply to traders who discount for defects and moisture. Since 97% of Cambodia’s cashew is exported raw, farmers have no fallback—any quality drop cuts income. Poor handling also blocks access to domestic processors and premium buyers, keeping farmers in low-value markets. Reducing post-harvest loss directly boosts earnings and opens doors to better markets, making it essential to address. This activity focuses on addressing critical post-harvest losses that currently reduce farmer incomes and limit market access. The project will establish 2 demonstration sites showcasing best practices in post-harvest handling, including proper drying techniques, storage methods, and quality grading systems. These demonstration sites will serve as learning centers for participating farmers and will be managed by the strongest Agricultural Cooperatives.
Activity 1.4: Lead institutional strengthening for ACs and PGs in Kampong Thom. SMP will work intensively with 1 selected Agricultural Cooperatives with 170 farmers to strengthen their institutional capacity and business management systems. This will include governance training for cooperative leaders, financial management system development, and business plan preparation. The cooperatives will receive support to develop internal control systems (ICS) that will enable them to access premium markets, including organic and fair-trade certificationpathways. ICS covers from the starting to the harvesting, following the standards/requirements of the audit/certificate to be certified. ICS implementation for organic certificate on rice – working closely with farmers for their records keeping throughout the production – planting, compost fertilizing, caring and harvesting which requires by auditor such as Control Union and EcoCert followingthe specific requirements of the certification.
Activity 1.5: Collect baseline and performance data for project evaluation. After SMP concludes their training and capacity building they will then go about collecting information to see the effectiveness of the training program. They will go to all their locations in both Kampung Thom and Lump hat. This informationwill also contribute to the final evaluation of the project where the project will also be presented to donors in Cambodia focused on Cashew Nuts (DFAT and EU).

participating-org.narrative: SANSOM MLUP PREY (SMP) was formed in 2009 to promote and market wildlife-friendly products grown or crafted in communities located in protected areas of Cambodia. It is working to link wildlife conservation to improving livelihoods of villagers limited by the constraints of living in a remote area with little opportunity to expand operations and access market. In Cambodia, protected areas either contain, or are used by, long-established local communities who are very poor and heavily dependent upon the forest and surrounding habitat for their livelihoods. Agricultural-based livelihood development is limited by low prices offered by the few traders that visit. This provides little incentive for communities to improve agricultural efficiency, and many households are trapped in debt cycles. With growing human population, the pressure on land resources is increasing, leading to widespread forest clearance in key conservation areas and conflicts between communities and government agencies responsible for environmental protection. Successful wildlife and habitat conservation depends on engaging them through tools that directly link local economic and social development to conservation. SMP buys products from village marketing networks (VMN), whose membersare voluntarily recruited from farmers who agree to abide by conservation rules and regulations, including wildlife protection and maintenance of land-use boundaries. These rules andregulations are previously concurred to by the government and the community. They offer preferential prices to community members, and target the poorer farmers, who are often not food secure and rely on forest resources. SMP plays a role as the villages connection to markets not typically accessible to producers from remoteprovinces and ensures that conservation activities are being adhered to, which enables rewards to be shared at the end of each season. SMP works in partnership with different organizations, including local and international NGOs, government ministries, andlocal villages.
